title: Cocartesian pullback preserves categorical equivalences
statement:
Use simplicial sets and degreewise pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $S$ and $Z$ be quasicategories in a fixed universe and let $r:Z\to S$ be a cocartesian fibration. Let $A,B$ be simplicial sets in that universe, let $b:B\to S$ be a simplicial map, and let $u:A\to B$ be a categorical equivalence; regard $A$ as a simplicial set over $S$ by $bu$. Then the induced map
$$u_Z:A\times_S Z\longrightarrow B\times_S Z$$
is a categorical equivalence. Neither $A$ nor $B$ is required to be a quasicategory, and no monomorphism hypothesis on $u$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 5.6.7.6, categorical-equivalence consequence, applied after pulling the cocartesian fibration back to B. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag; no Stacks theorem states this quasicategorical result. Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archived source.

proof.text: Use the family of relative Cartesian model structures of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model], in the fixed input universe. Its statement gives, for every small base, left proper combinatorial simplicial model structures, monomorphisms as cofibrations, the sharp-mapping-test weak equivalences, naturally marked cartesian fibrations as fibrant objects, the sharp simplicial enrichment, and the fiberwise and marked-homotopy-inverse criteria between fibrant objects. The tensor is $U\times K^\sharp$: currying a marked map $U\times K^\sharp\to V$ over a base $D$ is the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf M_D}(U\times K^\sharp,V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_D(U,V))$. On each simplex $\Delta^n\to K$ the curried map is the restriction $U\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to V$; these restrictions agree on faces and degeneracies, and conversely glue to the original marked map. It also gives the composition/pullback Quillen adjunction for every base map. These are exactly the family-of-model-structures hypotheses of the conditional Cartesian base-equivalence theorem used in step 4; no assertion about the present map has been used to discharge them.

source.place: Section 3.1.3; Corollary 3.1.4.4; the model structures preceding Proposition 3.3.1.3.

proof.text: For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ put $\rho(\alpha)(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$ for $0\leq i\leq m$. Then $\rho$ preserves identities and composition and satisfies $\rho^2=1$. Define $(K^{\mathrm{op}})_n=K_n$ and $K^{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)=K(\rho(\alpha))$. This involution preserves degreewise pullbacks. It exchanges the initial-edge horn condition with the final-edge horn condition, and exchanges the specified source of a cocartesian lift with the specified target of a cartesian lift. Thus $r^{\mathrm{op}}:Z^{\mathrm{op}}\to S^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cartesian by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Opposites preserve quasicategories, since the inner index $i$ becomes $n-i$. They preserve categorical equivalences in the testing convention of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]: there are natural identifications $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},C)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,C^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $h(D^{\mathrm{op}})=(hD)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The first comes from reversing both factors of $K\times\Delta^n$; the second reverses the generating edges and the composition relations from 2-simplices. Testing $u$ at $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and taking opposite ordinary categories therefore shows that $u^{\mathrm{op}}:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Opposite simplicial convention; dual of Proposition 3.3.1.3.

proof.text: Form $E=B^{\mathrm{op}}\times_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}Z^{\mathrm{op}}$ using $b^{\mathrm{op}}$, and let $q:E\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$ be its projection. The arbitrary-base pullback assertion of [lem-coef-relative-marked-anodyne-calculus] says that $q$ is a cartesian fibration. This applies even when $B$ is not a quasicategory: the cited statement explicitly uses the inner-fibration and final-horn definitions for arbitrary simplicial total spaces and bases. All sets remain small in the fixed universe.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.3 applied to a base-changed Cartesian fibration; arbitrary-base horn convention.

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of [lem-coef-cartesian-base-equivalence-invariance] to the cartesian fibration $q:E\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the categorical equivalence $u^{\mathrm{op}}:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to B^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its model-structure hypotheses were supplied in step 1; step 3 supplies its fibration hypothesis. Its statement requires neither base to be a quasicategory and does not require the equivalence to be a monomorphism. It follows that the projection $v:A^{\mathrm{op}}\times_{B^{\mathrm{op}}}E\to E$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.3 (the conditional form recorded in the cited existing DAG node).

proof.text: The degreewise bijection $(a,(b_0,z))\mapsto(a,z)$, whose inverse is $(a,z)\mapsto(a,(u^{\mathrm{op}}(a),z))$, identifies $A^{\mathrm{op}}\times_{B^{\mathrm{op}}}E$ with $A^{\mathrm{op}}\times_{S^{\mathrm{op}}}Z^{\mathrm{op}}$. It commutes with every simplicial operator and identifies $v$ with the map $(a,z)\mapsto(u^{\mathrm{op}}(a),z)$. Taking opposites therefore gives exactly $u_Z:(a,z)\mapsto(u(a),z)$, not just an unspecified equivalence of its source and target. For every quasicategory $C$, the restriction functor $h\operatorname{Fun}(B\times_S Z,C)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(A\times_S Z,C)$ identifies with the opposite of $h\operatorname{Fun}((B\times_S Z)^{\mathrm{op}},C^{\mathrm{op}})\to h\operatorname{Fun}((A\times_S Z)^{\mathrm{op}},C^{\mathrm{op}})$. The latter is an equivalence because it is restriction along $v$ after the displayed isomorphisms. Its opposite is an equivalence, which proves the required categorical-equivalence test. This proves the conclusion for the original arbitrary $A,B,u$.

source.place: Degreewise pullback identities and the opposite testing convention; dual of Proposition 3.3.1.3.
